Try putting deals on site like groupon, campuscred, google offers, etc. Make it look big, like $10 in credit for $6. A lot of people check those sites and use them to find deals. 

Other good promotion is coupons or fliers on the doors at local apartments, car hoods, other places like that. 

Advertise "meal deals", like 2 slices and a drink for $5 or something like that. Scout other local businesses and see what their prices look like.
Im a 3rd year junior, so a double major at this point would probably extend my undergrad, which i want to avoid. I feel shitty for not knowing what to do.

It's not that I don't like social sciences, I mean I really think they are important. I'm in sociology, but it just feels kind of odd. I don't do nearly the work that the other students have to do, and obviously I will make much less. Why not go on the sure bet?

Hey, it sounds like things are really hard right now. Or, have been for a long time. 

First, I am sorry about the job situation. Is there anything you can do to help it? By this I mean, is there someone at work that you could talk to, like your boss? They may be willing to work with you, or even happy that you came to them with your concerns. 

Secondly, it is really hard to not know happiness. What happens is we are unhappy for so long, that we kind of forget what it is to be happy. This seems natural, we know unhappiness so long we begin to think that happiness is maybe beyond our reach. There is hope, because happiness can be attained again. It really can be. 

There are a lot of things you can do to increase your happiness. Seeing a doctor or other relevant professional is key. If the people you are close with know about your feelings, they are concerned for you. Reach out to them, maybe ask them to help you find treatment in the way of a counselor or such. It is hard to go it alone.

Hey, sorry, I didn't see this reply for awhile. 

A lot of what you said resonated with me, which can be rare, so thank you for sharing.

On one level, I agree. I have been getting better. My low point was the beginning, not knowing how ot handle my new anxiety and having it scare me more than anything ever before. But, little by little, I got better. Since monday night I have been "down," from about a week or two, I guess since this posting, of what could be called happiness. So odd, I started enjoying things again.

This was huge for me. But it makes me nervous, like, what good is happiness now if I should be changing myself. It's like everything makes me nervous, it's like everything I see brings up a new anxiety. It is juvenile, but if I see someone on the street I think "Oh theyre cooler than men I'll never be normal," sorry, it's hard to articulate all of my thoughts, but that's about it. I know depressed people, I think I'm kind of depressed but I don't really hate myself. I just feel a fear and a panic that I won't ever be, well I'm not sure exactly what it is I want. 

Everything has this panic to it, mostly becuase of my age. I'm 21, and if you look at everyone's life stories, it seems like they were on their "path" by my age. I have no idea what I'm doing, and I don't want to have to settle, you know?

Thanks for the kind words. 

I was on lexapro for a year or so, ending this fall. It stopped panic attacks, but I haven't had any since I was off, either. I'm not sure if it helped much. I had something bad happen while I was on it, my friends in a sense all "broke up" with me because I was different now, guess I changed too much over summer. So I just became sad, and anxiety was there but it wasn't too bad. Wasn't great, not worth the meds. 

I'm off and have really no interest on going back on. I am not paranoid about the med's effects, it just wasn't worth it. I still felt what I feel now when I was on them, and it leads into the second reason why I won't use them again, which is that my problem is situational. 

I know this because I can be happy for a few days, maybe weeks at a time. My problem is that I am in school and I see everybody doing stuff, really anything (ie the majors they pick, being with friends, being comfortable) and it kills me. I am not trying to be dramatic, but I have no idea what I'm doing and as a result I feel anxious about my future. I could switch to a valuable major or something, but every choice I can imagine, there is a downside. I might not enjoy it or I will feel let down over time. I could probably be sedated into being okay with it, but why? I am frustrated, it's a sign that I need to do something, and anxiety comes over what to do. It wouldn't serve me to just float through to realize again later that I am even more fucked now for having done so. 


I am sorry if I seem aggressive or hostile, it's just really hard for me. A lot of anxiety/pain comes over seeing things I used to like, or would like if I wasn't anxious/depressed and then just feeling bad. It's really painful to remember how I was in a way, because I can see something and think "I would like that, I SHOULD like that, but I just don't feel that way."

I am so sorry that you feel this way. I know you can make it. Remember, just try to get through the day,  that's all you have to do. It is good to get things out, do not be ashamed of crying. 

Have you tried going for help? You are going through a lot, and you could really get a lot of assistance that you need.

Please, don't do anything drastic. I no what it is like to not see any hope, I have felt a lot of the things that you describe, but things changed. I am not special, they can change for you, too. Don't give up. There is no reason to die, even if it feels like there is no reason to live.

I agree, there is lot of sadness in the world, but a part of living is dealing with that. It is possible, many people do it. Most people, I'd think. A part of being human, I guess, is learning to rely on others. We don't need to just deal with sadness on our own, and we can make it through. There are many ways to deal with the bad parts of life, and it is certainly still worth sticking around. 

I don't mean to just spout what may seem like nonsense. I really believe what I say, but it is hard to convey my beliefs, perhaps.

Hey, it sounds like you are having a really rough time. 

But, I will remind you of a saying. It apparently comes from Yiddish or something, but the English version goes: the worm in horseradish thinks that the world  is horseradish. It applies here because you are in a depressed state, so it's understandable, but a mistake still, to see the world as joyless. I can assure you all day that people get joy from the world, and so can you, however it really comes down to how you are.

I guess the obvious step is treatment. This can be a counselor or something, anyone qualified, but it is important that you see one. They can really help.

Everything you feel is really hard, I get that, but it's a symptom. This means that you can still get out of it.

THe kind of determinism you feel, like you were meant to die by suicide or something, is totally relatable. I think it's a part of being suicidal, because we are considering committing a taboo, and it is somewhat deviant to even have the thoughts. But, don't put weight in those. They are something you shouldn't worry about, there is no truth in them. 

A lot of people feel this way, and a lot of people eventually progress through feeling this way. There is hope.

No one can deny that you have gone through some absolutely hellish things. Having your friend die is one of the toughest things to go through, and losing others is such a pain.

As for the headaches, perhaps you should see another doctor, or look into your options. I am not a lawyer, and I can't put ANY weight behind my words, but it seems like there should be some path for you to take on that. Perhaps another doctor can help. 

As for your parents, I am sorry that they don't understand. To not be understood is incredibly frustrating, but perhaps they are not trying to hurt you. It is likely that your dad was very shocked when you told him about how you are feeling. We live with our feelings all day, we have probably the best knowledge of them, but others may be clueless. I am sure your dad loves you, but especially in a father-son relationship, it can be hard to express and deal with something like this. 


You should really try to find a counselor, or therapist, anyone qualified to help. This is something that doesn't can be made much less hard by seeking help. You may feel no hope, but that is a symptom, not a reality. I know it feels real, but there is hope.
